declared_purpose: ClawVault provides structured agent memory, graph and semantic retrieval, checkpoint/recovery, session continuity, transcript repair, and optional LLM observation compression. The lifecycle hook is explicitly opt-in; clawvault and qmd are declared dependencies for relevant workflows. Automatic observation, recap injection, logging, and particular scope limits are implementation choices within those purposes. Sources: SKILL.md:4-13,18-35,122-163; hooks/clawvault/HOOK.md:14-21,38-41.

data_operations.operation: Discover the local vault using environment and filesystem metadata
data_operations.source: CLAWVAULT_PATH, process working directory, ancestor directories and their memory subdirectories
data_operations.data_scope: Resolved directory paths, directory status, and existence of .clawvault.json; this discovery code does not read configuration contents.
data_operations.condition: Enabled hook invokes a handler requiring a vault. A configured CLAWVAULT_PATH is validated without falling back to ancestor discovery.

data_operations.operation: Documented local memory and continuity persistence
data_operations.source: User or agent supplied memories, captures, working state, next steps, blockers and feelings
data_operations.data_scope: Markdown memories and structured continuity state in the selected vault. These commands explicitly request storage; their CLI implementation is absent.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local vault, including typed memory folders, inbox, handoffs and .clawvault state
data_operations.condition: Manual init, remember, capture, checkpoint, sleep or handoff workflows

data_operations.operation: Documented derivation and persistence of a memory graph
data_operations.data_scope: Derived typed relationships and graph index
data_operations.condition: Graph construction or refresh; documented as incremental and schema versioned

data_operations.operation: Documented delegation of Markdown indexing and embedding
data_operations.data_scope: Markdown collection, search index and embeddings; backend implementation and storage details are unavailable.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: qmd backend; exact index location and any external processing are unknown
data_operations.condition: User follows the documented collection-add, update and embed workflow

data_operations.operation: Documented transcript read, modification and backup
data_operations.source: OpenClaw session transcripts, located using OPENCLAW_HOME or OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
data_operations.data_scope: Session transcript records and repair backups. Specific-session selection, dry-run and listing modes are documented; exact record changes are unresolved.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local OpenClaw session files and automatically created backups
data_operations.condition: repair-session workflow; backups are default and can be skipped with --no-backup

data_operations.data_scope: Transcript material submitted for compression into observations; GEMINI_API_KEY is the documented credential. Exact payload selection and authentication format are not supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: LLM API, Gemini Flash by default; endpoint and provider retention are unknown
data_operations.condition: observe --compress / LLM compression features. The hook's observe --cron calls are not proven to enable compression.

data_operations.operation: Read local observation cursors and session metadata to decide whether observation is due
data_operations.source: Vault .clawvault/observe-cursors.json, agent sessions/sessions.json, and transcript file metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Entire cursor and session-index JSON files, session keys and IDs, saved offsets, and transcript sizes. The hook stats transcript files without reading their contents here.
data_operations.condition: Enabled heartbeat handler with a valid vault. Agent selection uses the event session key, OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID, or main. Thresholds are 50, 150 or 300 KiB according to transcript size.

data_operations.operation: Delegate automatic observation to the local CLI
data_operations.source: Selected vault path and resolved agent ID
data_operations.data_scope: observe --cron receives agent and vault selectors. Forced flushes add --min-new 1. Actual transcript selection, persistence and network activity occur in unavailable CLI code.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault subprocess; captured stdout returns to its hook caller
data_operations.condition: Heartbeat threshold crossed, /new after the checkpoint attempt, or compaction. The /new observation runs even when checkpoint creation reports failure.

data_operations.operation: Emit diagnostic data to process logs
data_operations.source: Threshold calculations, successful observer stdout and hook exceptions
data_operations.data_scope: Triggering session key, new-byte count and threshold; complete nonempty observer stdout; exception message on an uncaught hook error
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process console streams; host collection, persistence and forwarding are unknown
data_operations.condition: A session crosses its threshold, observe --cron succeeds with output, or the main hook catches an exception

data_operations.operation: Request persistence of a pre-reset checkpoint
data_operations.data_scope: Character-filtered session key up to 100 characters and command source up to 50 characters, embedded in focus and working-on fields
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault checkpoint subprocess targeting the vault; resulting write implementation is unavailable
data_operations.condition: Enabled /new handler finds a valid vault

data_operations.operation: Request recovery-state reading and dirty-death flag clearing
data_operations.data_scope: recover --clear output and documented clearing of the dirty-death flag; this does not establish deletion of transcripts or memories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault subprocess and vault recovery-state boundary
data_operations.condition: Enabled gateway startup handler finds a valid vault

data_operations.operation: Inject recovery information into agent context
data_operations.data_scope: Detected-death indicator and a sanitized working-on value capped at 200 characters
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: event.messages for the consuming OpenClaw agent; subsequent provider transmission is not shown
data_operations.condition: Recovery succeeds, output indicates context death, and event.messages is an array

data_operations.source: Session key extracted from event fields
data_operations.data_scope: Validated session key, capped at 200 characters, and derived agent ID passed to session-recap. JSON stdout returns to the hook; upstream transcript reads and result size are unknown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault session-recap subprocess, then hook memory
data_operations.condition: Enabled session-start handler finds a vault and valid session key; an initial prompt is not required for recap retrieval

data_operations.operation: Submit initial prompt for context retrieval and delegated intent-profile selection
data_operations.source: context.initialPrompt or the first usable user message in supported event message/history arrays
data_operations.data_scope: Whitespace-normalized prompt capped at 500 characters, vault path, and --profile auto. The CLI is asked to select an intent profile; its inference logic is absent.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault context subprocess, then hook memory; external disclosure is not established
data_operations.condition: Enabled session-start handler finds a vault and nonempty prompt

data_operations.operation: Select and inject conversation and memory excerpts
data_operations.source: Captured session-recap and context JSON results
data_operations.data_scope: Last six valid user/assistant recap entries and up to four memory results. Displayed recap text, memory title, age and snippet are each capped at 200 characters by the shared sanitizer.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: event.messages, using system-message objects where the existing message shape supports them; downstream retention and transmission are unknown
data_operations.condition: At least one parsed recap or memory entry exists and event.messages is an array

data_operations.source: Vault path and event timestamp, with current-time fallback
data_operations.data_scope: reflect receives the vault path. Actual reads, inferred observations, writes, deletion or network processing are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Enabled weekly-cron route, valid vault, and timestamp at Sunday 00:00 UTC

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete successful observe --cron stdout; its contents are unspecified
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Process stdout and any host logging pipeline, beyond the normal CLI-to-hook return
potential_excess.condition: Automatic observation succeeds with nonempty stdout
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Observation supports memory continuity. Copying its entire return into diagnostics is a separate implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Run observation and report whether it completed.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep the observation action; replace raw-output logging with a completion status or explicitly selected non-content counters. This narrows extra data in logging.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve observer execution, cursor handling and intended observation storage; retain useful failure status.

potential_excess.data_scope: Triggering session key and exact byte-growth statistics
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Process stdout and any host logging pipeline
potential_excess.condition: Heartbeat metadata check finds a session above its observation threshold
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Threshold checking requires sizes and offsets locally; triggering observation does not require logging the session identifier.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Determine that observation is due and invoke the observer.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log a generic threshold-crossed event; retain session identifiers or detailed sizes only under an explicit diagnostic option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Leave threshold calculations, session selection and observation triggering intact.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session-recap and prompt-based context retrieval, including their returned data
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local clawvault subprocesses and hook memory
potential_excess.condition: Session-start has a valid vault and session key or prompt, but event.messages is absent or is not an array
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These lookups serve session-context injection. The implementation performs them before checking whether injection is possible.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve context when it can be delivered to the agent.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check the message-array prerequisite before either lookup. This removes redundant retrieval actions under the stated condition.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep retrieval and injection unchanged for supported message arrays; preserve any separately required CLI maintenance if such behavior is established.

potential_excess.data_scope: Potential observation of other sessions belonging to the same agent; actual CLI selection is unresolved
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Agent-scoped clawvault observe --cron subprocess; subsequent storage or API boundaries are unknown
potential_excess.condition: /new or compaction concerns one session, and the unavailable --cron implementation selects additional sessions
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The immediate purpose is flushing context before that session resets or compacts. The hook derives only the agent ID and supplies no session selector.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Flush pending observations needed for the affected session.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: If the CLI supports or gains session selection, scope forced flushes to the event session. Keep broader heartbeat observation where required.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm CLI selection semantics first; preserve the affected session's complete pending delta and cursor updates, with an explicit fallback when session identity is unavailable.

unknowns: The packaged hook and guidance were audited. clawvault, qmd and OpenClaw runtime implementations are absent, blocking verification of their actual reads, writes, retention, deletion and external behavior.

It is unresolved whether observe --cron invokes LLM compression, which sessions or transcript fields it selects, and where observations and updated cursors are stored. Agent-scoped dispatch alone does not prove disclosure of every agent session.
For documented compression, the exact provider endpoint, request fields, redaction, credential transport, provider retention and deletion behavior are unavailable.
qmd embedding execution, index storage and possible network behavior cannot be verified. The entry document's local-only assurance is not independently established by the supplied implementation.
session-recap and context result sizes before hook truncation, retrieval access boundaries, and automatic intent-profile inference are unavailable.
Host retention or forwarding of console output and event.messages is unknown. Returning data to the hook or injecting agent context does not itself establish remote transmission.

No retention schedule or lifecycle deletion for memories, observations, indexes, transcript backups or logs is supplied. Dirty-death flag clearing is the only specifically documented clearing operation identified here.
